digest.key_takeaway: Cloudflare, VoidZero and Max Schwenk announced tsrs, an experimental Rust port of the TypeScript compiler, built with the TypeScript team's involvement. Cloudflare claims up to 8x faster checking and 70% less memory than TypeScript 7.0, though one test against 7.1 beta showed 2.7x. It lacks watch mode and a language server, and exits with code 2 on type errors. By Daniel Curtis

articles.title: All Types of Caching in .NET: When to Use Each (Deep Dive, Part 1)
articles.summary:
Your API is slow and Claude recommends you to add caching.

It adds IMemoryCache to the shipment tracking API, and the p95 latency drops from 120 ms to 5 ms.

Everyone is happy.

Then they scale to two instances.

A customer updates the delivery address, refreshes the page, and sees the old one.
Refreshes again and sees the new one. One more refresh, and the old address is back.

Nothing is broken. Each instance has its own memory, and only one of them knows that the address has changed.

articles.title: Your First Reproduction Is Usually Wrong: A Receipt-Before-Patch Workflow for OSS Fixes
articles.summary:
A contributor opens a pull request against a parser library with a failing test, a two-line fix, and a confident description of the bug. The test goes red on their machine, green after the patch, and the maintainer merges it after a quick skim. Six weeks later the same crash reappears in a downstream project, because the original test never actually depended on the code that was changed. articles.title: PLC Programming in Modern Manufacturing: Practical Approaches for Reliable Control Systems
articles.summary:
When a production line stops unexpectedly, the first suspicion usually falls on hardware: a failed sensor, a worn actuator, a loose connection. Often, though, the real obstacle is the control logic itself. It may be undocumented, inconsistent, or so tangled that nobody can safely change it. That is why PLC programming deserves the same attention as mechanical and electrical design. This article explains what it involves, which languages and methods suit different tasks, and what manufacturers should consider to keep control software dependable over the life of a machine.

articles.summary: I've been building a predictive coding (PC) engine from scratch in C++20, with a thin Python layer on top, and just cut the first public release. Posting here for feedback and because I haven't seen many from-scratch PC implementations with real kernel-level optimization work behind them. articles.title: Cloudflare’s Auto Router Rates Each Request for Stakes, from the Most Recent Turns
articles.summary: Cloudflare has released Auto Router in public beta through AI Gateway, picking a model per request from a classifier that scores complexity, ambiguity, stakes and context dependence. Cloudflare’s own benchmark puts it ten points below Claude Opus 5.5 on success rate at a third of the cost, and practitioners have questioned how stakes survive a long agent session. By Steef-Jan Wiggers
